items.prompt: Which prefix makes the opposite of possible?

options.why: Unpossible is not a real word. Try saying it aloud.
Dispossible is not a real word.
Ir- goes before words that start with r, like irregular.

hints: Say each new word aloud. Only one is a word you have heard.
Think of other words that start with p, such as polite and patient. How do you say their opposites?
Start with un + possible. Does that sound right? Then try the next prefix.
items.explanation: Impossible means not possible. Words that start with p, b or m usually take im- for the opposite, like impolite and imbalance.

items.prompt: Add a prefix to legal to make a word that means against the law.
hints: Look at the first letter of legal.
Words that begin with l often take a prefix that ends in l, like logical and illogical.
Write the prefix first, then write legal straight after it with no gap.
items.explanation: Illegal means against the law. Words starting with l take il-, so the new word has a double l: il + legal.

items.prompt: Match each prefix to its meaning.
hints: Think of a word you know with each prefix, such as rewrite or submarine.
Ask yourself what the prefix adds to the meaning of the word you thought of.
Start with re-. What does it mean to rewrite a story?
items.explanation: Rewrite means write again, preview means see before and misspell means spell wrongly. A submarine goes under the sea, international means between nations and antibacterial soap works against germs.

items.prompt: Add a suffix to music to name a person who plays music.
hints: Think of the word for a person who does magic tricks.
Words ending in c often take -cian when they name a person or a job.
Write music, then add the ending that sounds like shun.
items.explanation: Music ends in c, so the word for the person ends in -cian: musician, like magician and electrician.

items.prompt: Sort the words by the prefix that makes their opposite.
hints: Look carefully at the first letter of each word.
Il- goes before l, ir- before r and im- before p, b or m. Many other words take in-.
Start with regular. Say its opposite aloud and listen to how it begins.
items.explanation: The opposites are impatient, immature, irresponsible, irregular, illogical, illegible, invisible and incorrect. The prefix often matches the first letter of the word.

items.prompt: Add -ous to make two adjectives. courage: ___ fame: ___
hints: Both words end in e. Notice what happens to that e in each new word.
Keep the e after g so that the g still sounds like j. In most other words the e is dropped.
Say courage aloud. Is the g hard, as in got, or soft, as in giant?
items.explanation: Courageous keeps its e so the g stays soft. Fame drops the e before -ous, giving famous.

items.prompt: Which ending completes both words? sens___ and poss___

options.why: -able usually follows a whole word, like enjoyable. Sens and poss are not whole words.
Sensous and possous are not words. Try saying them aloud.
Sensful and possful are not words.

hints: Notice that sens and poss are not words on their own.
-able usually follows a complete word, like enjoy. Think about which ending is used when the start is not a word.
Try each ending on poss and say the word aloud.
items.explanation: Sensible and possible both end in -ible. The -ible ending often follows a part that is not a whole word, while -able often follows a whole word, like enjoyable.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct spelling?

options.why: Verbs ending in -de, like explode, usually change to -sion, not -tion.
The -ian ending is used for people, like musician.
The shun sound is not spelt -shun at the end of English words.

hints: Look closely at the end of the long word in each sentence.
Think of the verb this noun comes from: explode. Verbs ending in -de often change in the same way.
Compare it with decide and decision. Which ending matches?
items.explanation: Explode becomes explosion, just as decide becomes decision. Verbs ending in -de usually change to -sion.

items.prompt: Choose all the words where a final e was dropped before the suffix was added.

options.why: Excite keeps its e because -ment starts with a consonant.
Use keeps its e because -ful starts with a consonant.
Care keeps its e: care + ful.

hints: Work out the root word inside each word first.
A final e is usually dropped when the suffix starts with a vowel, and kept when it starts with a consonant.
Start with the first word. What is its root word, and does the suffix start with a vowel?
items.explanation: Hope, write and fame lose their e before -ing and -ous, which start with vowels. Excite, use and care keep their e because -ment and -ful start with consonants.

items.prompt: Simple becomes simply when -ly is added. Which word follows the same spelling rule?

options.why: Happy changes y to i before -ly. That is a different rule.
Sad just adds -ly with no change.
Love just adds -ly, and the e stays.

hints: Look at the last two letters of simple.
Simple ends in -le. Look for another root word that also ends in -le.
Write the root word of each option and check how it ends.
items.explanation: Gentle and simple both end in -le, so the -le changes to -ly: gently, simply. Happily, sadly and lovely follow different rules.

items.prompt: Add -ful to the word in brackets. Be ___ on the wet stairs. (care)
hints: The suffix goes on the end of the root word.
Care plus ful makes a new word.
Write care, then add the ending -ful.
items.explanation: Care + ful makes careful, which means taking care.

items.prompt: Which word is made by adding a prefix to a root word?

options.why: Red is a whole word. It has no prefix.
Real is a root word on its own. The re is not a prefix here.
Reed is a plant. It is not re + ed.

hints: A prefix comes at the start of a word.
Take the first letters off. Is a smaller real word left?
Try redo: take off re. Is do a word?
items.explanation: Redo is re + do. The prefix re- means again.

items.prompt: Amara ___ the instructions, so her model did not work.
hints: The prefix must change the meaning to wrongly.
Unread means not yet read. Think about which prefix means wrongly or badly.
Try each word in the sentence and check that it is a real word.
items.explanation: Mis- means wrongly. Misread means read wrongly.

items.prompt: Build the sentence.
hints: Start with the word Please.
Recheck means check again.
The describing word carefully goes last.
items.explanation: Recheck is re- + check, so it means check again.

items.prompt: Sort the words by their suffix.
hints: Look at the last letters of each word.
Both suffixes make nouns.
Find the cards that end in ness first.
items.explanation: The suffix -ness joins kind, dark and happy. The suffix -ment joins move, agree and pay.

items.prompt: Match each suffix to its meaning.
hints: Think of a word you know with each ending.
Hopeless means without hope.
Start with -less and -ful, they are opposites.
items.explanation: Hopeless means without hope, hopeful means full of hope, readable means can be read, and a singer is a person who sings.

items.prompt: Choose the word that fits. The ___ of the new bridge took two years.

options.why: Constructive is an adjective. It describes something helpful, so it cannot follow The here.
A constructor is a person. A person cannot be the thing that took two years.
Construct is a verb. We need a noun after The.

hints: The word after The must be a noun that names a job being done.
The suffix -tion often makes a noun from a verb.
Try each word and ask: is it a noun that means the act of building?
items.explanation: The suffix -tion turns the verb construct into the noun construction, the act of building.

items.prompt: Complete the table.
head: Word
Prefix
Root word
hints: Prefix plus root word makes the whole word.
Read each row from left to right.
Row 2 has prefix dis and root agree. Put them together.
items.explanation: Disagree is dis + agree. Preheat is pre + heat.

items.prompt: Add -ly to the word full. Write the new word. ___
hints: Full is an adjective. Adding -ly makes an adverb.
Count how many l letters the new word has.
Full already ends in ll. One l is dropped before ly.
items.explanation: Full + ly drops one l, so it is spelled fully.

items.prompt: Put the words in the order they are built.
hints: Start with the root word.
Add the suffix before the prefix.
Then add the prefix, and last change the ending to -ly.
items.explanation: Comfort + able = comfortable. Add un- to get uncomfortable. Change the ending to get uncomfortably.

items.prompt: Choose all the words that start with a prefix meaning not.

options.why: Re- means again, not not.
Pre- means before, not not.

hints: The prefixes im-, ir-, il- and in- can all mean not.
Say each word with the meaning not at the start.
Rule out the words where the prefix means again or before.
items.explanation: Impossible, irregular, illegal and incorrect all mean not. Re- means again and pre- means before.

items.prompt: Wulan wrote about her ___ when she won the prize. Which spelling is correct?

options.why: Happy ends in y after a consonant. The y changes to i before -ness.
There is only one n before the double s.
Keep both p letters from happy.

hints: Look at the last letter of the root word happy.
A y after a consonant changes to i before most suffixes.
Change y to i, then add -ness.
items.explanation: Happy becomes happi- before the suffix, so happy + ness is happiness.

items.prompt: Spell the word that means not necessary.
items.sentence: It is unnecessary to bring a coat today.
hints: The word starts with the prefix un.
The root word has one c and two s letters.
Say un, then spell necessary: n, e, c, e, s, s, a, r, y.
items.explanation: Unnecessary is un- + necessary. Both the n of un and the n of necessary stay.

items.prompt: Which word begins with the letters un but does NOT have the prefix un-?

options.why: Unfair is un- + fair.
Unwrap is un- + wrap.
Undo is un- + do.

hints: A prefix is added to a word you can already say on its own.
Take off un. Is a real word left?
Check what is left of each word after taking off un.
items.explanation: Uncle is not un- + cle. Cle is not a word, so un is not a prefix there.

items.prompt: Begin plus -ing doubles the n to make beginning. Which word follows the same spelling rule?

options.why: The stress in visit is on the first part, so the t is not doubled.
The stress in offer is on the first part, so the r is not doubled.
The stress in happen is on the first part, so the n is not doubled.

hints: Say each root word and listen for the strong beat.
The consonant doubles when the last part of the root word is stressed.
Begin is be-GIN. Which root word also has the strong beat at the end?
items.explanation: Forget is for-GET, with the stress at the end, so the t doubles before -ing.

items.prompt: Add -ly to careful. Write the new word. ___
hints: The word careful already ends in -ful.
Only add the letters ly.
When -ful gets -ly, you end up with -fully.
items.explanation: Careful plus -ly makes carefully. The suffix -ful has one l, but -fully has two.

items.prompt: Which spelling is correct?

options.why: The suffix -ful has only one l.
The suffix -ful has only one l.
The suffix -ful has only one l.

hints: The word full has two l letters.
When it is a suffix, it loses one.
Choose the word with a single l at the end.
items.explanation: As a suffix, -ful has only one l: helpful.

items.prompt: Use the root word and prefix. What does misjudge mean?

options.why: That would be rejudge.
That would be prejudge.
Mis- means wrongly, not not at all.

hints: Find the root word first.
Mis- is a prefix that means wrongly.
Put the meaning of mis- together with judge.
items.explanation: Mis- means wrongly, so misjudge means to judge wrongly.

items.prompt: Read: "The explorer was reluctant to leave the warm cabin, so she lingered by the fire." What does reluctant mean?

options.why: She stayed by the fire, so she was not excited.
She could leave, but did not want to.
The sentence is about what she wanted, not what she was allowed.

hints: Look at what she did next.
She stayed by the fire.
Think about why someone stays in a warm place.
items.explanation: She stayed by the fire, so she did not want to go. Reluctant means unwilling.

items.prompt: Read: "The glass was so transparent that Sekar could see the fish clearly." What does transparent mean?

options.why: The sentence is about seeing, not weight.
Nothing says the glass is fragile.
If she could see the fish clearly, the glass had no strong colour.

hints: The clue is what Sekar could do.
She could see the fish clearly.
What must the glass be like if you can see through it?
items.explanation: If Sekar could see the fish clearly, the glass must be easy to see through.

items.prompt: Sort the words by what happens when -ing is added.
hints: Short words with one vowel then one consonant often double.
Words ending in two consonants stay the same.
Words with an unstressed last syllable do not double.
items.explanation: Run, stop and plan have a short vowel then one consonant, so the last letter doubles. Jump, visit and help do not.

items.prompt: True or false: The prefix un- in the word unfair changes the meaning to the opposite of fair.
hints: A prefix goes at the start of a word.
Un- often means not.
Think of unkind and unhappy.
items.explanation: Un- means not. Unfair means not fair.

items.prompt: True or false: Adding the prefix re- to the word play makes a word that means play less.
hints: Think of replay a video.
Re- means again.
It does not mean less.
items.explanation: Re- means again, so replay means play again.

items.prompt: True or false: The suffix -ful in the word helpful means full of.
hints: Look at the ending.
Think of joyful and painful.
Ful sounds like full.
items.explanation: Helpful means full of help. Care plus -ful gives careful.

items.prompt: True or false: Adding the suffix -ly to the word happy gives the spelling happyly.
hints: Look at the letter before the y.
The y changes.
Y becomes i.
items.explanation: When a word ends in a consonant plus y, change the y to i before -ly. The spelling is happily.

items.prompt: True or false: The prefix in- changes to im- before the letter p, as in impossible.
hints: Look at the first letter of possible.
Compare with impatient.
Try saying inpossible.
items.explanation: Words that begin with p, m or b often take im-. In- becomes im- before p.

items.prompt: True or false: The word irregular is made by adding the prefix im- to regular.
hints: Look at the first letter of regular.
Which prefix goes with r?
Think of irresponsible.
items.explanation: Irregular is made with ir-, which is used before words that begin with r.

items.prompt: Add ir- to regular: ___.
hints: Ir means not.
Put ir at the front.
ir + regular
items.explanation: Ir- means not, so irregular means not regular.
